title: serving-runtime-daily-scratchpad-2026-03-26
content:
Daily scratchpad - serving-runtime (personal)

Goals for today:
- Triage incoming bugs from yesterday's rollout (canary -> global)
- Run kernel A/B with 2x batch sizes on p4d to validate latency tail impact
- Follow up on KV cache eviction issue (seen on long-chat sessions)
- Quick writeup for kernel-selector heuristic improvement idea

Bug triage (priority order):
1) JIRA-RT-4821: tokenization mismatch for abrupt-stop responses (reported by QA)
   - Repro: model: redwood-13b-v1, prompt with multi-seg streaming + stop tokens sometimes ignored
   - Observed: stop token not honored intermittently when streaming chunk boundary aligns with token boundary
   - Hypothesis: streaming flush + tokenizer buffer edge-case (race when partial token emitted)
   - Next: add repro unit test -> reproduce locally with minimal stream size -> instrument StreamWriter flush timing
   - Owner: me (Samira) -> ETA EOD to reproduce

2) JIRA-RT-4878: KV cache growth on long sessions (customer reported memory spike)
   - Notes: happens >8k tokens, memory climbs > reserved margin, eviction not triggered until GC pause
   - Immediate mitigation: enforce soft cap on session tokens (configurable) + emit eviction telemetry (per-session)
   - Perf experiment: enable bounded-KV-evict with window=4096 and run load test; compare QPS and p99
   - Stakeholders: eng-sre, applied-ml (for evals)

Perf TODOs / experiments:
- Kernel A/B (p4d) - compare default-kernel vs kernel-opt-3 (AVX + fused attention patch)
  - Metrics: p50, p95, p99 latency for seq_len=1024 and seq_len=4096; throughput tokens/s; GPU util; power
- Batching profile: simulate real mix (chat gen 70%, embed 20%, rerank 10%) and tune batcher window
- Micro-optim: reduce mutex contention in KV cache map by sharding map (4 -> 16 shards) -> instrument lock hold times
- Plan: run one hour per config with 50 concurrent sessions, collect traces, upload to perf bucket

Kernel notes / ideas:
- kernel-selector heuristic: current uses model_arch + avg_seq_len. Idea: incorporate recent-seq-length-distribution (last N requests) and hardware thermal headroom. If avg seq grows > threshold, bias toward kernel with better long-seq memory locality even if slightly worse p50.
- Heuristic fields to add: recent_p95_seq, gpu_temp_baseline, fraction_streaming_requests, quantized_preference_score
- Quick pseudocode (for later PR):
  - score = w1 * model_fit + w2 * recent_p95_seq_norm + w3 * thermal_penalty + w4 * quant_pref
  - pick kernel with max score but ensure fallback chain for run-time errors

Notes to self / misc:
- Add debug flag to emitter to include per-token timings when rt_log_level=debug (only for dev env)
- Reminder: follow up with Diego about dedicated autoscale test for burst=3x capacity (Thu)
- Slack threads to check: #serving-runtime (kernel-opt), #sre-ops (memory spike alert), #prod-issues (customer anchor)

Meeting follow-ups:
- Sync with Applied ML 11:00am: confirm that fused-attention changes don't alter logits for redwood-13b-v1 eval set
- Post-mortem draft for yesterday's canary slowdowns -> start doc skeleton, include timeline and JVM metrics

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are we confident the streaming writer flush rate is the real cause for stop-token bug? need repro with deterministic flush intervals
- What's the risk of sharding KV map on memory fragmentation for long sessions? ask infra team

Quick TODO checklist (tick when done):
- [ ] Reproduce JIRA-RT-4821 locally with a small harness
- [ ] Launch kernel A/B jobs on p4d-12 for seq=4096
- [ ] Add eviction telemetry to session events 
- [ ] Draft kernel-selector proposal doc and post to PRD reviews

Last tested:
- Local load (simulated chat) -> p50 48ms, p95 132ms, p99 210ms (seq len 1024)
- Canaries yesterday showed 12% tail increase at p99 on one region (investigating)

Misc links (for reference):
- perf dashboard: https://perf.redwood.internal/dashboards/serving-runtime
- related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/892
- jira: https://jira.redwood.internal/browse/RT-4821

End of scratchpad.
